Safety plus golden fit and variety gates. No LLM judges safety anywhere.

25 tests across desktop, 375px and 320px. Baseline was 51 (e2e-public.txt); v11 added rendered-copy, header geometry/disclosure/zoom and landing-proof assertions. The header exemption is gone, so this run does certify the header. Two intermittent failures were seen once each during v11 and did not reproduce on re-run — see blocker P2-SUITE-FLAKES.

PARTIAL. Six journeys (login, settings data controls, pricing trial state) now genuinely execute against the live Supabase project as a synthetic account, across desktop / 375px / 320px — the first authenticated execution at this baseline. Six remain skipped: they require the trial-eligible and trial-used fixtures, which MW-V11-04 added to the seed script but which have not been seeded here (running the service-role seed is not permitted in this session). Each skip now names the exact fixture and command, so it can no longer be mistaken for a decision. This is recorded as a pass only for the six that ran.

BLOCKED for the same reason as e2e-authenticated. Every one of the eight seeded states now asserts page identity and that the fixture actually applied before testing anything, so a seed that silently fails to apply produces a failure rather than a state assertion that passes for the wrong reason.
Fails closed without production env pulled, by design. Owner must run it with the real environment; it prints presence only and never a value.

First performance measurement in the project's history. Lab, not field: 4x CPU throttle, ~Slow 4G, cold browser cache against a warmed server. Landing LCP 812ms, pricing 600ms, signup 612ms against a 2500ms budget; CLS 0 on all three against a 0.1 budget. INP is NOT measured — the recorded interaction probe is a labelled proxy and must not be reported as INP. Cold-start is excluded and remains a separate risk: the first request to a cold route measured 4080ms LCP versus 812ms warm.
Opt-in and advisory by design. It cannot gate a release and is never counted as a pass.

blockers.title: The product renders in Arial, not its brand typeface. Geist was loaded but never applied — `body` sets Arial and no component uses `font-sans` — so 53KB of webfonts were downloaded and never painted.
blockers.acceptance: An explicit decision: keep the system stack, or adopt Geist deliberately. MW-V11-05 removed the unused download rather than changing the typeface, because altering the type of every screen is a design decision and not launch hardening.

blockers.title: Three different suites have each failed once under full-suite load and passed on re-run: tests/email-templates.test.ts (6.1s for pure Intl formatting), the public keyboard-tabbing journey (60s timeout), and tests/content-system.test.ts (5.7s scanning customer surfaces). All three are slow-then-fail, never fail-fast, and none reproduces in isolation or on a re-run.
blockers.acceptance: Root cause identified and fixed, or the reads made resilient. NOT to be closed with a retry or a longer timeout. Diagnosis so far: the first theory (CPU contention from a concurrent production build) is now weaker, because the content-system failure happened with nothing else running. The common factor across all three is heavy synchronous filesystem reads under parallel vitest workers on Windows. The associated risk is worse than the flake itself: a doc-scanning test that asserts the ABSENCE of a phrase passes trivially if the read returns empty, so a partial read could produce a false green rather than a failure. MW-V11-07 added non-empty guards to the new doc-scanning tests; the pre-existing ones have not been audited for this.

rollback: Flag-based and data-safe. FLAG_MONTHLY_FAIR_USE=0, FLAG_PLAN_REPAIR=0, FLAG_WEEKLY_REFLECTION=0, FLAG_EMPHASIZE_YEARLY unset, FLAG_TRIAL_LENGTH_EXPERIMENT=0 (pinned trials complete exactly as disclosed; no subscription is touched), plus per-surface UI reverts. Every migration in the repository is additive and re-runnable, so no migration reversal is required to roll back any behaviour.
